title: Model deprecation handling and version handoff
content:
Purpose and scope:

Quick working doc to capture UI/UX wireframe notes, microcopy variations and backlog items for how the Console should show model deprecation, help teams hand off pinned versions, and create endpoint-level safeguards when a pinned model is scheduled for deprecation. Focused on the model catalog + endpoint creation flows and the pin lifecycle (pin -> deprecate notice -> handoff / migrate / rollback).

Audience: product designers, PMs, eng owners for pinning + runtime routing, docs writers, solutions eng.

Context / problem statement (short):
- We currently allow pinning a model version to an endpoint. When a model version is deprecated upstream (e.g., vendor/OSS maintainer marks it EOL or we want to withdraw a quantized variant), customers need a clear, non-surprising experience.
- Missing pieces: explicit deprecation notices on endpoints, a handoff flow for owners to pick replacement variants, automated migration suggestions (e.g., compatible variant list), and copy for all states.

Design goals (prioritized):
1) Avoid silent breakage. Endpoint requests should not unexpectedly start failing because a model variant was retired.
2) Make migration low-friction: default safe suggestions + quick test call sandbox.
3) Surface ownership and risk (who owns this pin? when will it be unavailable?).
4) Provide safe rollback and canary options.
5) Accessible and concise microcopy for banners/modals.

Wireframe notes (sketch descriptions, left-to-right):
- Model catalog entry (compact card): badge row includes: [stable | community] + version badge + small triple-dot menu. Add a tiny clock icon when version is scheduled for deprecation and an inline hover tooltip: "Deprecated variant — scheduled removal 2025-04-15. Click to see endpoints using this variant."
- Variant details pane: header shows full semantic version, release date, compatibility score (0-100), and a small "migration score" calculated from evaluation runs for common workloads. Under the header: two columns. Left: description + known differences. Right: endpoints using this variant (list). For any endpoint that is pinned to this variant we show owner, last deploy, and a colored risk pill (green/yellow/red) with reason.
- Endpoint detail banner (top of page when pinned version is deprecated or scheduled): compact banner (info -> warning -> critical) with a single strong CTA and two secondary actions. Example layout: [yellow warning icon] "Pinned model version v1.3.2 will be retired 2025-04-15. This endpoint will lose access on that date unless you pick a replacement." CTA1: "Choose replacement" (opens handoff modal). CTA2: "Schedule auto-fallback" (choose fallback variant + date).
- Handoff modal (primary interaction): three-step inline wizard: 1) Choose replacement (preselected recommended variant with reasoning), 2) Run smoke test (single-request runner that executes your last known prompt or sample), 3) Confirm swap (canary options: 5% traffic for 24h, or immediate swap).
- Confirmation / safety: when swapping, show impact estimate (token cost delta, latency delta) based on historical metrics for the endpoint. Also provide a "preview of last 5 outputs" matrix when running smoke tests.

Microcopy drafts (variants, short):
- Deprecation banner (warning):
  - Option A (concise): "Pinned version v1.3.2 will be retired on Apr 15, 2025. Pick a replacement to keep this endpoint running."
  - Option B (friendly): "Heads up — the model version powering this endpoint is being retired on Apr 15, 2025. Choose a replacement or schedule a fallback to avoid interruption."
  - Option C (urgent): "Action needed — your endpoint is pinned to a retiring model. Choose a replacement now or traffic will fail after Apr 15, 2025."

- Handoff modal title examples:
  - "Select replacement for v1.3.2"
  - "Migrate endpoint to a supported variant"

- Replacement recommendation blurb (short):
  - "Recommended: v1.4.0 — closest match on accuracy and latency (diff +2% latency, +0.8% accuracy)"

- Confirm swap CTA text: "Migrate endpoint" vs "Start canary" — decision: use "Start canary" when selecting non-zero percent, otherwise "Migrate endpoint". Keep verbs consistent.

- Auto-fallback description (in banner/tooltip):
  - "If you enable auto-fallback, when the pinned variant is removed we will automatically switch to a compatible variant you approve and notify the endpoint owner."

Failure modes and copy:
- If replacement fails smoke test: "Migration blocked — recommended replacement failed smoke tests. Try a different variant or run a custom test."
- If user ignores deprecation and date passes: two-step behavior: 1) soft-fail window (72 hours) where requests return a descriptive 503 with header 'model-retired' containing migration suggestion link; 2) hard-disable after escalation (admin-mode only) if no action. Copy for 503: "This endpoint’s pinned model version has been retired. Request blocked. Visit the endpoint page to select a replacement or enable fallback."

Accessibility and localization notes: 
- Banners must meet contrast AA. Use icons + text. Screen reader should expose deprecation date and CTA labels.
- Modal flows must be keyboard-trap safe and have cancel/back controls with clear labels.
- Copy variants checked for 80 char lines for translations. Leave placeholders for dates/timezones (show user's timezone).

Backlog grooming items (rough):
- PROD-607: Catalog UI: show deprecation badge on variant card (2 d).
- ENG-3245: Endpoint banner wiring + API flags for 'deprecation_scheduled' (5 d).
- DES-112: Handoff modal prototype + copy (3 d).
- QA-78: Smoke test runner integration + sample prompt persistence (4 d).
- SRE-19: Soft-fail 503 behavior + header hooks (3 d).
- DOCS-45: Public docs and email template for customers (2 d).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- When a variant has deprecation metadata (date + reason) the catalog shows a visible badge and endpoints list shows an endpoint-level banner.
- Handoff modal allows selecting a replacement variant, running a single-sample smoke test, and confirming a swap with canary percent. Swap triggers a deploy event and shows cost/latency delta.
- If swap fails smoke test, the console surface explains why and prevents immediate migration.
- Soft-fail behavior for requests during the initial post-deprecation window returns a descriptive 503 and an admin alert.

Open questions / decisions: 
- Default recommended replacement algorithm: should we bias toward same quantization & similar latency or toward highest accuracy? (tradeoffs for cost-sensitive customers).
- Should we allow endpoint-level policy: "always auto-migrate to highest compatibility"? If yes, add policy toggle in endpoint advanced settings.
- Communications: should we send automatic emails to endpoint owner 30 / 14 / 7 / 1 days before deprecation? Who is 'owner' when endpoint is shared across teams?

Suggested copy for email (short):
Subject: Action needed: model version v1.3.2 powering your endpoint will be retired
Body (first lines): "Hi <owner>, the model variant v1.3.2 used by endpoint <name> is scheduled for retirement on Apr 15, 2025. Visit the endpoint settings to choose a replacement or enable auto-fallback. We recommend running the smoke test on any replacement before migrating."

Edge-case flows to capture in follow-ups:
- Multiple endpoints pinned to same variant — bulk migration UI (list + bulk-confirm).
- Pin owned by service account / automation — who gets emailed? Add root team contact fallback.
- Customer-managed private deployments: exportable migration plan for ops teams (CSV listing endpoints, owners, suggested replacements).

Design explorations to try (A/B):
- Banner CTA label: "Choose replacement" vs "Resolve deprecation" -> test for fewer clicks to migration.
- Inline auto-suggest: show two ranked replacements (one cost-optimized, one accuracy-optimized) vs single recommendation.

Loose wireframe checklist for handoff modal (developer handoff note):
- [ ] 1) Modal header + variant info snippet
- [ ] 2) Recommended replacement card (small metrics) + alternative list
- [ ] 3) Smoke test runner area (sample prompt + run button + past outputs table)
- [ ] 4) Canary config (percent dropdown) + traffic routing note
- [ ] 5) Cost/latency delta estimator (based on historical data)
- [ ] 6) Confirm/migrate CTA + cancel

Notes from last sync (2/20):
- Engineering flagged that we need new API field deprecation_date and deprecation_reason on model-version resource.
- SRE insists on a 3-day soft-fail grace window by default to give customers time to react.
- Solutions Eng asked for export CSV for large accounts.

Next steps (this doc):
- Turn wireframe into Figma quick mock (DES-112) — assignee: Marco. Due: 2025-03-12.
- Draft API spec for deprecation metadata — assignee: Omar. Due: 2025-03-06.
- Draft email template and doc snippet for support site — assignee: Priya. Due: 2025-03-09.

Misc shorthand + brainstorm fragments (keep for historical context — rough):
- "what if we auto-route to hosted-compatible variant in non-prod orgs?"
- "should rate-limits change on fallback? sometimes fallback is more expensive"
- "consider 'pin-protection' flag in Dedicated contracts: customer must opt-in for auto-migration"

End of doc.
